newsitem.title: USA: Bob Hope ends 60 year relationship with NBC.
newsitem.headline: Bob Hope ends 60 year relationship with NBC.

text.p: Comedian Bob Hope declared on Wednesday he is ending his 60-year relationship with NBC and becoming a "free agent."

"Guess what? I've decided to become a FREE AGENT! ... So, watch out Michael Jordan!" the 93-year-old Hope wrote in a full-page ad in Hollywood trade papers. "I've enjoyed 60 memorable years with NBC. Sixty years ... I started before the peacock -- and he wound up taking my parking space."
Hope, considered a consummate master of timing who turned the one-line joke into an art form, did not say what he planned to do after his contract ends with NBC.

He made his radio debut on the "Capitol Family Hour" in 1932. Soon after hosting his first NBC broadcast in 1935 for Bromo Seltzer he was signed to do his own radio show, which continued until 1956. Hope began on NBC television in 1950.
The English-born comic, one of few performers to succeed in five mediums -- vaudeville, stage, radio, movies and television -- was honoured in May 1996 for his career in TV.
On Nov. 23, Hope will air his final NBC special, "Laughing With the Presidents," a retrospective of his relationships with American presidents over the years.
